copy.bis:

copy.bis: Kung bugnaw ang palibot, mahinay molihok ang mga mananap nga bugnaw og dugo kay monaog usab ang init sa ilang lawas.

copy.bis: Sa kolloid, kasarangan ang gidak-on sa mga partikulo mao nga nagpabilin kini nga nagsabit ug dili molugdang!

copy.en:
What causes color blindness?

A normal retina has three kinds of cones for red, green, and blue; when one kind is missing or weak, a person becomes color blind.
copy.tl:
Ano ang sanhi ng color blindness?

Ang normal na retina ay may tatlong uri ng cones para sa pula, berde, at asul; kapag kulang o mahina ang isa, nagkakaroon ng color blindness.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang hinungdan sa color blindness?

Ang normal nga retina adunay tulo ka matang sa cones alang sa pula, berde, ug asul; kung kulang o huyang ang usa, mahimong color blind.

copy.tl: Sa tatlo, ang pugita at cuttlefish ang pinakamabilis magpalit ng kulay dahil gumagamit ng kalamnan, samantalang mas mabagal ang chameleon na umaasa sa kristal.
copy.bis: Sa tulo, ang kugita ug cuttlefish ang pinakapaspas mag-usab og kolor kay mogamit og kaunoran, samtang mas hinay ang chameleon nga nagsalig sa kristal.

copy.en:
Why does the colugo glide at night?

The colugo usually glides at night because darkness makes it harder for predators to spot it as it crosses between trees.
copy.tl:
Bakit gabi lumilipad ang colugo?

Karaniwang lumilipad ang colugo kapag gabi dahil mas mahirap itong makita ng mandaragit sa dilim habang tumatawid ito sa pagitan ng mga puno.
copy.bis:
Ngano gabii molupad ang colugo?

Kasagaran molupad-lupad ang colugo kon gabii tungod kay mas lisod kini makita sa manunukob sa kangitngit samtang motabok kini tali sa mga kahoy.

copy.en:
Is the flying lemur really a lemur?

Nope! The Philippine flying lemur, or kagwang, is not a true lemur — and it doesn't really fly either.
copy.tl:
Totoo bang lemur ang kagwang?

Hindi pala! Ang Philippine flying lemur o kagwang ay hindi tunay na lemur, at hindi rin talaga ito lumilipad.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga lemur ang kagwang?

Dili diay! Ang Philippine flying lemur o kagwang dili tinuod nga lemur, ug dili gyud kini molupad.

The kagwang, found gliding through the forests of Mindanao.

Kagwang, na matatagpuan sa mga kagubatan ng Mindanao.

Kagwang, nga makita sa mga kalasangan sa Mindanao.

copy.en: When a bird builds its nest on a tree branch, it gets a safe home, while the tree is neither helped nor harmed — this is called commensalism.
copy.tl: Kapag nagpupugad ang ibon sa sanga ng puno, nakakakuha ito ng ligtas na tirahan, samantalang ang puno ay hindi natutulungan o nasasaktan — commensalism ang tawag dito.
copy.bis: Kung mosalag ang langgam sa sanga sa kahoy, makakuha kini og luwas nga puy-anan, samtang ang kahoy dili matabangan o madaot — commensalism ang tawag niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 'Commensalism' comes from Latin words meaning 'sharing a table'
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en:
What does 'commensalism' really mean?

'Commensalism' comes from Latin words meaning 'sharing a table' — because one animal often eats another's leftovers.
copy.tl:
Ano talaga ang ibig sabihin ng commensalism?

Ang 'commensalism' ay galing sa Latin na nangangahulugang 'pagsasalo sa isang mesa' — dahil madalas, kumakain ang isang hayop ng tira ng iba.
copy.bis:
Unsa gyud ang buot ipasabot sa commensalism?

Ang 'commensalism' gikan sa Latin nga nagpasabot og 'pag-ambit sa usa ka lamesa' — kay sagad, mokaon ang usa ka hayop sa salin sa lain.

copy.en:
How can you stop a cold from spreading?

A cold spreads easily from person to person, so covering your mouth when you cough or sneeze and washing your hands often help stop it.
copy.tl:
Paano hindi kumakalat ang sipon sa ibang tao?

Madaling kumakalat ang sipon mula sa isang tao patungo sa iba, kaya nakakatulong ang pagtatakip ng bibig kapag umuubo at madalas na paghuhugas ng kamay.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nga dili mokatap ang sip-on sa uban?

Ang sip-on dali mokatap gikan sa usa ka tawo ngadto sa uban, mao nga makatabang ang pagtabon sa baba kung mag-ubo ug ang kanunay nga paghugas sa kamot.

copy.tl:

Tumutulong ang kompas! Ipinapakita nito sa mga marino ang tamang direksiyon kahit walang landmark.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpangita og dalan sa mga marinero bisan walay timailhan?

Nagtabang ang compass! Nagpakita kini sa mga marinero sa husto nga direksiyon bisan walay timailhan.

copy.en: A flower with all four of its parts is called a complete flower. If even one part is missing, it's incomplete.
copy.tl: Ang bulaklak na may lahat ng apat na bahagi nito ay tinatawag na kumpletong bulaklak. Kapag may kulang kahit isa, ito ay hindi kumpleto.
copy.bis: Ang buwak nga adunay tanan sa upat ka bahin niini gitawag og kompleto nga buwak. Kon adunay kulang bisan usa, kini dili kompleto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Egg, larva, pupa, and adult
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card lists the four stages of complete metamorphosis but does not use a flow chart and does not compare life cycles across animals (butterfly, frog, chicken, human) as required. It only provides background about one type of life cycle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Egg, larva, pupa, and adult
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, and plants. The card describes insect complete metamorphosis, which is not among the specified groups, and does not compare life cycles.

copy.en:
What are the four stages of complete metamorphosis?

Egg, larva, pupa, and adult — that's the full journey of complete metamorphosis!
copy.tl:
Ano ang apat na yugto ng buong metamorphosis?

Itlog, uod (larva), pupa, at matandang insekto — iyan ang buong daan ng complete metamorphosis!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang upat ka hugna sa kompletong metamorphosis?

Itlog, ulod (larva), pupa, ug hamtong nga insekto — mao kana ang tibuok agianan sa kompletong metamorphosis!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The four-stage change that includes a chrysalis is called complete metamorphosis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card names complete metamorphosis but does not use a flow chart to compare life-cycle stages, which is the required format and action of G4-L-5. It provides background vocabulary about one type of insect life cycle, not a comparison of stages across animals.

copy.en:
What is the four-stage bug change called?

The four-stage change that includes a chrysalis is called complete metamorphosis — bees and beetles go through it too.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag sa apat na yugtong pagbabago?

Ang pagbabagong may apat na yugto at chrysalis ay tinatawag na kumpletong metamorphosis — dinadaanan din ito ng pukyutan at salagubang.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang tawag sa upat ka hugna nga kausaban?

Ang kausaban nga adunay upat ka hugna ug chrysalis gitawag og kompleto nga metamorphosis — agian usab kini sa putyukan ug bakukang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Complete metamorphosis has four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the four stages of complete metamorphosis but does not use a flow chart or compare life-cycle stages as required by the competency. It provides related vocabulary but no direct instructional support for the flow-chart comparison skill.

copy.en: Complete metamorphosis has four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult.
copy.tl: Ang ganap na metamorphosis ay may apat na yugto: itlog, larva (uod), pupa (chrysalis), at adult.
copy.bis: Ang kompleto nga metamorphosis adunay upat ka yugto: itlog, larva (ulod), pupa (chrysalis), ug hamtong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When it turns dark, crumbly like soil, and smells fresh and earthy instead of like rotting trash
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes physical signs of finished compost (dark, crumbly, earthy smell) but does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting, or being degradable/biodegradable. Compost is a result of decomposition, but the card does not teach the chemical property itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When it turns dark, crumbly like soil, and smells fresh and earthy instead of like rotting trash
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about recognizing finished compost, not about proper handling or disposal of materials according to their properties (reusing, disposing of oil, recycling). It does not demonstrate any handling or disposal action.

copy.en:
How can you tell compost is finished?

When it turns dark, crumbly like soil, and smells fresh and earthy instead of like rotting trash — that means it's ready for the garden.
copy.tl:
Paano mo malalaman na tapos na ang compost?

Kapag maitim na ito, durog-durog na parang lupa, at amoy-sariwang lupa na — hindi na amoy-basura — handa na itong ihalo sa lupang taniman.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nimo masayod nga human na ang compost?

Kon itom na kini, durog-durog nga morag yuta, ug humot nga morag yuta — dili na baho — andam na kini isagol sa yuta sa tanaman.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Compost returns nutrients to the soil so plants can grow stronger and healthier
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in a guided investigation to identify the effect of different types of soil on the growth of plants
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not a guided investigation of how different soil types affect plant growth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Compost returns nutrients to the soil so plants can grow stronger and healthier
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Nutrients in soil are not observing leaves, roots, and stems and their role to get water and nutrients.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Compost returns nutrients to the soil so plants can grow stronger and healthier
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Compost as fertilizer is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: Compost returns nutrients to the soil so plants can grow stronger and healthier.
copy.tl: Ibinabalik ng compost ang mga sustansya sa lupa para mas malusog na tumubo ang mga halaman.
copy.bis: Ang compost mobalik sa mga sustansya ngadto sa yuta aron molambo og maayo ang mga tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Worm castings are packed with nutrients like nitrogen, so mixing them into soil makes plants grow healthier and faster
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Worm castings as fertilizer is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: Worm castings are packed with nutrients like nitrogen, so mixing them into soil makes plants grow healthier and faster — nature's own fertilizer.
copy.tl: Punong-puno ng sustansya tulad ng nitrogen ang casting ng bulate, kaya't paghalo nito sa lupa ay pinapalusog at pinapabilis ang paglaki ng halaman — likas na pataba.
copy.bis: Puno kaayo sa sustansya sama sa nitrogen ang casting sa ulod, mao nga ang pagsagol niini sa yuta makapalig-on ug makapadali sa pagtubo sa tanom — natural nga abono.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An escalator is a cool compound machine!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The competency G6-F-1 asks students to observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines. This card explicitly describes an escalator as a compound machine, not a simple machine, and does not identify or explain any simple machine components (lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane, wedge, screw). It shares the broad topic of machines but provides no direct instructional support for identifying or describing simple machines.

copy.en: An escalator is a cool compound machine! A motor drives gears that move a continuous chain, carrying the steps up or down in a never-ending loop.
copy.tl: Ang escalator ay isang compound machine! Ang motor ay nagpapaikot ng mga gear na nagpapagalaw ng chain, nagdadala ng mga baitang pataas o pababa sa isang loop.
copy.bis: Ang escalator usa ka compound machine! Usa ka motor nagmaneho sa mga gear nga nagpalihok sa padayon nga chain, nagdala sa mga baitang pataas o pababa sa usa ka loop.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pump compresses air into a smaller space and pushes it into the tyre at higher pressure.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses air being compressed and pressure, but does not describe the shape and volume properties of gases (no definite shape or volume) nor contrast solids/liquids/gases. It only touches on gas volume change indirectly, not the competency's core content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pump compresses air into a smaller space and pushes it into the tyre at higher pressure.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air (a gas) but does not identify the three states of matter or that matter exists as solids, liquids, and gases. It focuses on compression and pressure, not on the existence of three states.

copy.en:
Why does a bicycle pump get harder to push as the tyre fills up?

The pump compresses air into a smaller space and pushes it into the tyre at higher pressure. As the tyre fills, the high pressure inside makes pushing the plunger harder!
copy.tl:
Bakit nahihirapan mong i-push ang bicycle pump habang puno na ang gulong?

Kino-compress ng pump ang hangin sa maliit na espasyo at itinutulak sa gulong sa mas mataas na presyon. Habang puno ang gulong, mas mahirap itulak ang plunger dahil mataas na ang presyon!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas lisod iduso ang bicycle pump kung hapit puno na ang gulong?

Gicompress sa pump ang hangin sa mas gamay nga espasyo ug giduso sa gulong sa mas taas nga presyon. Kung puno na ang gulong, mas lisod iduso ang plunger tungod sa taas nga presyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A solution with lots of solute in a little water is concentrated and strong-tasting. Adding more water makes it dilute and weaker-tasting!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: express quantitatively the amount of solute present in a given volume of solvent
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes concentration qualitatively (concentrated vs dilute) and does not express the amount of solute quantitatively in a given volume of solvent, which is the core action of G7-M-9. No units, ratios, or quantitative measures are provided.

copy.en: A solution with lots of solute in a little water is concentrated and strong-tasting. Adding more water makes it dilute and weaker-tasting!
copy.tl: Ang solusyon na maraming solute sa kaunting tubig ay concentrated at matapang ang lasa. Kapag dinagdagan ng tubig, nagiging dilute at manipis ang lasa!
copy.bis: Ang solusyon nga adunay daghang solute sa diyutayng tubig kay concentrated ug lig-on og lasa. Kon dugangan og tubig, mahimo kining dilute ug nipis og lasa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Concorde was a passenger jet that flew at Mach 2, about 2,180 km/h — twice the speed of sound!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a specific speed value but does not explain the concept of speed as distance traveled per unit time. It provides no information about distance, time, or the relationship between them, so it does not directly support the competency's goal of identifying what speed is.

copy.en: The Concorde was a passenger jet that flew at Mach 2, about 2,180 km/h — twice the speed of sound!
copy.tl: Ang Concorde ay isang eroplanong pampasahero na lumipad sa Mach 2, halos 2,180 km/h — doble ng bilis ng tunog!
copy.bis: Ang Concorde usa ka eroplano sa mga pasahero nga milupad sa Mach 2, mga 2,180 km/h — doble sa tulin sa tingog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mix cement, sand, gravel, and water to make concrete!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a mixture (concrete) but does not describe it as uniform or non-uniform, nor does it mention solutions or suspensions. It only states the ingredients and that it hardens, which is not directly teaching the classification of mixtures.

copy.en: Mix cement, sand, gravel, and water to make concrete! It starts soft and squishy, but hardens into a super strong material.
copy.tl: Paghaluin ang semento, buhangin, graba, at tubig para sa konkreto! Malambot ito sa simula, pero titigas at magiging napakatibay.
copy.bis: Isagol ang semento, balas, graba, ug tubig para sa konkreto! Humok kini sa sinugdanan, apan mogahi ug mahimong lig-on kaayo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: shoot venom like a tiny harpoon to catch their prey
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a feeding behavior (shooting venom to catch prey) but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. It is only tangentially about an animal's body and feeding.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: catch their prey
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card indicates the cone snail is a meat eater (catches prey) but does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to classify. It only provides a single example of a carnivorous behavior.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: shoot venom like a tiny harpoon to catch their prey
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a predatory adaptation (venomous harpoon-like structure) but does not explain how the animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it mention mimicry or camouflage. It is an example of an adaptation but lacks the evolutionary/environmental context required by the competency.

copy.en: Some sea snails called cone snails, living in Philippine seas, shoot venom like a tiny harpoon to catch their prey.
copy.tl: May mga suso na tinatawag na cone snail sa karagatan ng Pilipinas na nagpapana ng makamandag na lason para hulihin ang biktima nito.
copy.bis: Adunay mga kuhol nga gitawag og cone snail sa kadagatan sa Pilipinas nga nagpana og hilo sama sa bangkaw aron dakpon ang tukbonon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A constellation is a group of stars that forms a pattern or shape when seen in the sky!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only defines what a constellation is. It does not explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions or verify seasons, nor does it mention directions, seasons, or cultural reliance. The definition is shared vocabulary but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Ever wonder how stars make pictures in the sky?

A constellation is a group of stars that forms a pattern or shape when seen in the sky!
copy.tl:
Napapaisip ka ba kung paano gumagawa ng mga larawan ang mga bituin sa langit?

Ang konstelasyon ay isang grupo ng mga bituin na bumubuo ng pattern o hugis kapag tinitingnan sa langit!
copy.bis:
Natinghup ba ka kung giunsa paghimo sa mga bituon ug mga litrato sa langit?

Ang konstelasyon usa ka pundok sa mga bituon nga nagahimo ug pattern o porma kung tan-awon sa langit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In the house, the control panel distributes power through wires in the walls to different outlets and switches.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a household control panel distributing power, which is related to electrical circuits but does not support the competency's focus on guided investigations to infer relationships among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits. It provides no instruction on circuit assembly, measurement, or data interpretation.

copy.en: In the house, the control panel distributes power through wires in the walls to different outlets and switches.
copy.tl: Sa bahay, ang control panel ay namamahagi ng kuryente sa pamamagitan ng mga wire sa dingding papunta sa iba't ibang outlet at switch.
copy.bis: Sa balay, ang control panel nag-apod-apod sa kuryente pinaagi sa mga wire sa bungbong padulong sa lain-laing outlet ug switch.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so your heartbeat slows gradually
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a practical cool-down tip after exercise, mentioning heartbeat slowing and gentle stretching. It does not describe how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work, which is the required competency. The mention of heartbeat is only a health-related outcome, not an explanation of circulatory system function.

copy.en: After exercising, cool down with slow walking and gentle stretching so your heartbeat slows gradually and you don't feel dizzy.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos mag-ehersisyo, mahalagang magpalamig nang dahan-dahan sa pamamagitan ng mabagal na paglakad at pag-uunat, upang unti-unting bumagal ang tibok ng puso at hindi mahilo.
copy.bis: Human magpa-ehersisyo, hinay-hinay ang pagpabugnaw pinaagi sa hinay nga paglakaw ug pag-inat, aron hinay-hinay nga mohinay ang pitik sa kasingkasing ug dili malipong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thick wire gives electricity a wider path! It carries a stronger current without overheating
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses copper wire thickness and current capacity, but does not address designing/constructing a circuit to test which materials conduct electricity or identifying conductors/insulators. It shares the topic of electricity but provides no direct support for the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A thick wire gives electricity a wider path! It carries a stronger current without overheating
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that thicker wire carries more current, which touches on resistance, but it does not involve guided investigations, series/parallel circuits, or inferring the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance. It is background knowledge about wire gauge, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why are some copper wires thicker?

A thick wire gives electricity a wider path! It carries a stronger current without overheating, which is why big appliances like air conditioners use them.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas makapal ang ibang tansong wire?

Mas malaki ang daanan ng kuryente sa makapal na wire! Kaya kayang magdala ng malakas na kuryente nang hindi umiinit, kaya ginagamit ito ng malalaking appliance.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas baga ang ubang tumbaga nga wire?

Mas dako ang agianan sa kuryente sa baga nga wire! Makadala kini og mas kusog nga kuryente nga dili mainit, mao nga mogamit og baga nga wire ang dagkong appliance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They're relatives of jellyfish and sea anemones — they all share the same stinging tentacles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Related stinging invertebrates are not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they all share the same stinging tentacles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: Stinging tentacles are not head, legs or wings used to move and gather food.

copy.en:
What are coral polyps related to?

They're relatives of jellyfish and sea anemones — they all share the same stinging tentacles!
copy.tl:
Kamag-anak ng ano ang coral polyp?

Kamag-anak ito ng dikya at sea anemone — pareho silang may galamay na nakakapaso!
copy.bis:
Kaparyente ba sa unsa ang coral polyp?

Kaparyente kini sa dikya ug sea anemone — silang tanan adunay galamay nga makapaso!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Much of it comes from crushed coral and limestone, broken up by waves and some fish!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sand formation from crushed coral/limestone, not soil formation from rocks and minerals. It touches on rock breakdown but does not explain soil formation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: broken up by waves and some fish!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions waves breaking up material (erosion) but does not demonstrate or describe transport of Earth materials. No movement or deposition is addressed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Much of it comes from crushed coral and limestone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions limestone as a rock type but does not involve observing/collecting rocks or comparing features like texture, color, or grain size. It is only a passing reference.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Much of it comes from crushed coral and limestone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions non-living materials (limestone, sand) but does not involve guided activities to locate and describe non-living things in and around school. It is a general earth-materials fact, not aligned with the grade 3 activity.

copy.en:
Where does all that white beach sand come from?

Much of it comes from crushed coral and limestone, broken up by waves and some fish!
copy.tl:
Saan nagmula ang puting buhangin sa beach?

Marami dito ay nagmula sa durog na coral at limestone, dinurog ng mga alon at ilang isda!
copy.bis:
Asa naggikan ang puti nga balas sa baybay?

Daghan niini naggikan sa dugmok nga coral ug limestone, gidugmok sa mga balod ug pipila ka isda!
